- I: A statement (we can assume it's true or false)
- H: Another statement (we can assume it's true or false)
- ~I: NOT I
- ~H: NOT H
- I ≡ ~H: I if and only if ~H

| I | H | ~I | ~H | I ≡ ~H | ~I | ~H | ~I ≡ H | ~(~I ≡ H) |
| T | T | F | F | F | F | F | T | F |
| T | F | F | T | T | F | T | F |
| F | T | T | F | F | T | F | T |
| F | F | T | T | T | F | T | F |

From the truth tables, we can see that the propositions I ≡ ~H and ~(~I ≡ H) are never true at the same time. So, they are contradictory.

However, they are not logically equivalent because they are not always true at the same time. So, the answer is (G).
